subject.title: Enhancement: Allow custom safe headers in fetch-guard cross-origin redirects

question: Should OpenClaw allow operator-configured custom request headers to be retained across cross-origin redirects, and if so should the scope be per-origin or per-caller rather than a global safe-header list?
rationale: The requested change intentionally relaxes a credential-exfiltration guard and adds config surface, which repository policy treats as security/product-sensitive.

options.title: Design scoped opt-in
options.body: Add an explicit opt-in that is constrained by redirect target/origin and caller surface, with auditability and tests for secret-like headers.

options.title: Keep fixed core allowlist
options.body: Leave core strict and document that integrations needing custom redirect auth must own redirect handling or avoid cross-origin redirects.

options.title: Defer to broader fetch-auth design
options.body: Handle this together with the related auth-forwarding policy work so OpenClaw has one credential-forwarding model.

recommendation.title: Design scoped opt-in
recommendation.body: Add an explicit opt-in that is constrained by redirect target/origin and caller surface, with auditability and tests for secret-like headers.

likelyOwner.reason: The central security hardening history for fetch-guard traces to this owner path.
